question: Which remaining Android node capability should OpenClaw accept in core, and under what security boundary: narrow device.control, ADB/system.run-like access, dynamic Kotlin execution, or none for now?
rationale: Source inspection can prove the remaining capabilities are absent, but only maintainers can choose the permanent trust, policy, and product boundary for remote Android device control and code execution.

options.title: Narrow Device Control First
options.body: Accept explicit foreground/permission-gated Android device-control commands and defer ADB and dynamic execution until a stronger execution policy exists.

options.title: Route Through Execution Protocol
options.body: Wait for or coordinate with node-hosted tools and system.run-style approval design before adding broad ADB or dynamic execution.

options.title: Keep Core Closed For Now
options.body: Ask contributors to keep ADB and dynamic execution in external experiments until OpenClaw has an approved Android remote-execution security model.

recommendation.title: Narrow Device Control First
recommendation.body: Accept explicit foreground/permission-gated Android device-control commands and defer ADB and dynamic execution until a stronger execution policy exists.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus reviewed and landed the relevant Android node/session work and already made the clearest product-direction statement on Android session defaults.
